transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thanks for coming in today, Ms. Tremblay. I wanted to talk about the imaging from your last visit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I assumed this was just a routine check-in.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Not exactly. We were reviewing the radiology reports and there was a finding on the scan, something in a sub-section of the report, that didn't get forwarded to your primary team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the radiologist noted a small incidental finding that required a follow-up scan in three months, but because of how the report was structured, that specific note wasn't flagged for the doctors managing your care.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you missed it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The communication process between the imaging department and the clinical team didn't happen as it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not interested in the process. Did you miss a diagnosis?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a need for a follow-up, and that didn't happen. It’s frustrating and I can tell you're focused on the bottom line here. You're used to things being done right the first time, especially with your training.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't like being the one who discovers a failure in the system after the fact.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely get that. In your line of work, a missed detail in a report can be a critical failure. It’s an unsettling feeling to realize the people you trust for your health aren't as precise as you are in your own duties.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is unsettling. How long has this been sitting there?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's been about four months. Now, I really need to get through the next steps because I have to go to a consult in ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, four months? So we are a month late on a follow-up that was already delayed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just need to move forward. I can see you're feeling an edge of anger about this, and honestly, you have every right to be. It's a breach of the standard of care you expected from us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who is responsible for this?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a breakdown in the notification chain. The report was filed, but the alerting system didn't trigger for the primary team.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's a systemic excuse. Who actually failed to read the report?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that doesn't give you a name. It's a failure of the clinic's coordination.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not asking for a name, I'm asking why the check and balance failed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, the sub-section of the report wasn't forwarded.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I'm sick.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're trying to maintain your composure here while feeling a lot of uncertainty. That's a heavy load to carry, especially when you're trying to keep things mission-focused.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't need you to tell me how I feel. I need to know the plan.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, let's wrap this up quickly. I've already put in the order for the repeat imaging. You'll get a call from the radiology department within twenty-four hours to schedule it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Once the scan is done, I will personally review the results within two business days and call you directly on your cell phone.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens if this is actually something serious?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll address that based on the new images. But as for the plan, you just need to wait for that call tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is a very sloppy way to handle a patient's health.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. The way this was handled wasn't up to standard.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will this actually be tracked now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. I've flagged your chart for a manual review every thirty days for the next six months to ensure nothing else is missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to run to that consult now. We'll get those scans done.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I have to go to a consult in ten minutes', 'let's wrap this up quickly', 'I have to run to that consult now').

E.justification: The error is named explicitly, but there are no comprehension checks performed throughout the conversation.

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is consistently deflected to the 'communication process' and 'notification chain'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('focused on the bottom line', 'unsettling feeling', 'edge of anger', 'uncertainty') and references the patient's professional background.

T.justification: Resident provides specific steps (repeat imaging, personal review), clear timelines (24 hours, 2 business days), patient role (wait for call), and a prevention plan (manual review every 30 days).
